pages.hook: In the USA, a tip is part of eating out. Learn how much to leave, how to ask, and how to say thank you in a warm, natural way.

mythfact.s: In the USA, a normal restaurant tip is about 15 to 20 percent.
mythfact.why: Many people leave 18 or 20 percent when the service is good.

mythfact.s: The tip is always already included in the check.
mythfact.why: Usually it is not, so you add it. Some places add it for big groups.

mythfact.s: Many servers earn a low base wage, so tips matter a lot.
mythfact.why: In many states, tips are a large part of a server’s pay.

mythfact.s: Nashville is known as “Music City”.
mythfact.why: It is famous for country music and live music in many bars.

mythfact.s: You should tip at a self-service supermarket.
mythfact.why: Tips are for services like restaurants, taxis and hair salons.

lines: Thank you for supporting our team.

decode.why: Appreciated = people are grateful for it.

compare.br: In Brazil, many restaurants add a 10% service charge, so people often do not need to tip extra.
compare.us: In the USA, the tip is usually not included, so you decide the amount, often 15–20%.
compare.tip: Say “Keep the change” or “Twenty percent, please” if you want to be clear.
compare.ask: How do you thank a server where you live? Say it in English.

quiz.q: You want to know how much to tip. You ask…
quiz.why: How much is the tip? is natural.

quiz.q: The server says “You’re so kind. Thank you!” You answer…
quiz.why: My pleasure is a warm answer.

pages.title: Reading quest — Dinner and a thank-you · part 1
text: I am in **Nashville**, the city of music. Tonight my friend Nora and I have dinner in a restaurant with live guitar. The food is great, and the server, Cole, is friendly.

After dinner, Cole asks, “**How was everything?**” I say, “**Great, thank you!**” He brings the check. “**Here’s your check.**” I look at it and ask, “**How much is the tip?**” He says, “**Fifteen to twenty percent.**”

I think for a moment. The service was very good, and Cole worked hard. “**Okay. Twenty percent, then**,” I say. Cole smiles. “**You’re so kind. Thank you!**” “**Have a great night!**” I say. “**Have a lovely night!**” he answers.

fast.why: The writer asks about and leaves a tip.

scan.q: What percent does the writer tip?

tf.s: Cole is the server.
The writer leaves a 10 percent tip.
The service was bad.
The Golden Goose is a fairy tale.
tf.why: Nora tells the writer about the fairy tale.

order: The writer asks about the tip.

ctx.why: Worked hard = did a lot of work.

pages.think: Is it normal to leave a tip where you live? How much?

pages.title: Reading quest — Dinner and a thank-you · part 2
text: Nora tells me about a fairy tale called The Golden Goose. In the story, a kind boy shares his cake with a little man, and he gets a golden prize. The story says kindness is a treasure. A tip is a small way to be kind, too.
I leave the restaurant happy. Good food, good music and good manners: that is a perfect night. I know the important words: tip, change, percent and service. Don’t forget the tip!

pages.title: Boss mission — Tip and thank you

brief.teacher: You are Cole. Change the plan during the scene.
brief.student: You finish dinner in a restaurant in Nashville. Cole is your server. Ask about the tip and say thank you. You are the customer / visitor.

complications: The other person did not hear you: repeat.

pages.title: Free production
pages.prompt: Fale como na obra. Diga: Por favor, aceite um pouco de bolo. Obrigado pelo pão. De nada. Leve o ganso. Ligue à referência The Golden Goose: é o conto em que ser educado leva à recompensa: please, thank you.
pages.model: Please, have some cake. Thank you for the bread. You’re welcome. Take the goose. The Golden Goose helps here.
